examples.label: Reference — certutil UA vs PowerShell UA
examples.command:
# certutil:  User-Agent: Microsoft-CryptoAPI/10.0
# powershell: User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT...) WindowsPowerShell/5.1
# Spoof with: $UserAgent = [PSUserAgent]::Chrome

notes:
Invoke-WebRequest -> Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT ...) WindowsPowerShell/5.1...
WinHttpRequest -> Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; Win32; WinHttp.WinHttpRequest.5)
Msxml2.XMLHTTP -> Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; ... Trident/7.0 ...)
certutil -> Microsoft-CryptoAPI/10.0
BITS -> Microsoft BITS/7.8
Detections: command-line allow/deny-listing, User-Agent analysis, SIEM correlation. Every built-in Windows transfer tool leaves a distinct User-Agent. Proxy logs + Sysmon are the primary detection controls. Living-off-the-land (certutil/bitsadmin) blends better than raw PowerShell UA. Encrypted channels (HTTPS) defeat content inspection but not behavioral analytics. Also covered in: CPTS Ch07 (File Transfers).
name: Reference - Transfer Method User-Agents
